mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rates (below 0.5%) signal sustained monetary accommodation that compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for two consecutive months indicates labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal broad demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of 60-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%) triggers anticipated Federal Reserve tightening that increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) declining below 100 for three consecutive months signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100 for three months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% YoY) indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days without conditional triggers.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of 5-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) during late-cycle expansions (GDP growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 5.0%) signal sustained consumer confidence that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST rises during late-cycle expansion.
